surfaces.part: stone brick wall/floor tile surface with moss and vines

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 64x64 tiling texture, with a silhouette width of 64 on every row. It shows a flat pattern of stone slabs with mortar lines and moss patches, with no object silhouette, no front face and no top surface band. The kind is terrain, so it is a seamless ground or floor tile and not a standing object. The repeated horizontal mortar lines every 16 rows and the vertical joints form a flat brick pattern with no eave shadow or ellipse.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a paving of pale stone slabs with green overgrowth tufts, so it matches the ground kind. Measured facts favour it: 11 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass reference, 15% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the joints and vine lines are tinted brown or green rather than black. By eye the slabs carry only about 3-4 steps of beige (light, mid, shadow, joint) and little per-stone grain. Most of the texture comes from the green tufts, and the slab faces are fairly smooth. The reference paving shows cobble dots and a bevelled highlight and shadow on every slab, which is more detailed. The 15% flat coverage and the sparse slab shading make it look slightly thinner than the references. It is decent, but a careful artist would likely want more grain and shading on the stone faces.

surfaces.part: stone brick floor with moss and cracks, a flat tiling texture

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 64x64 tile of stone bricks with mortar lines, moss patches and dark cracks. It is a seamless terrain texture with no silhouette, no standing body, no front face and no top surface to measure. The brick courses are seen flat (head-on, or from above). The standing-object rules do not apply, so the reading is other (terrain tile).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a cream-beige flagstone floor with green vines and moss tufts, which fits the ground kind and sits next to the grass and paving references. Measured facts support it: 11 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 15%, low but above the references' 0%, and 13% exact flat fill is small. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the joint and crack lines lean brown or green rather than black, which reads as dark_material_tone. By eye, the stone blocks show about 5 steps (highlight, light, mid, shadow, joint). Each block has speckle and grain, and the green moss clumps use several greens. The flat areas are limited to some block interiors, so texture is 'some' rather than 'rich'. It is slightly simpler than the cobble-shaded paving reference, which shades stones one by one, but it is not sticker-like and a careful artist would accept it next to the references.
